prerequisites: Knowledge of cinematic codes and/or audio and video technologies

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module will have a comprehensive theoretical and practical foundational knowledge of the aesthetic design rules of film language.
Through macrostructural analyses of exemplary film excerpts, students will have detailed knowledge in selected areas and genres of film theory.

Students can apply the acquired theoretical knowledge of cinematic design rules in the production and evaluation of their own practical work. The experimental projects are carried out in small groups.

As part of short presentations, students present cinematic impact analyses in a well-structured and strongly media-supported form. During the presentation, they subject a selected cinematic work to the rules, concepts, and discussion results developed in the course. Individual presentation competence is jointly assessed and improved after the presentations. As part of the practicals, students develop strong teamwork skills through conceptual work, filming, and post-production in small groups.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the history and analysis of film
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either a project report (10-15 pages with an 8-10 minute presentation) or a presentation (approx. 15 minutes). The ungraded assessment is an experimental work, consisting of approximately 10 hours of design work over 2 months within the context of the course.
